title: Picard-zero square defect on a semiabelian group is trivial over the ground field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $H/k$ a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume that over an algebraic closure $\bar k$ there is an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $1\to\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}^r\to H_{\bar k}\to A\to1$, where $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}\bar k[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication, and $A$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected commutative group scheme [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-pc-base-change, def-pc-fppf-site]. Let $T$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_H$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Assume $T_{\bar k}$ is algebraically equivalent to $\mathcal O_{H_{\bar k}}$, meaning that their classes are related by a chain of pairs of fibres of invertible-module families on $H_{\bar k}\times V$, with $V$ a smooth connected $\bar k$-variety. Write $m:H\times_kH\to H$ for multiplication and $p_1,p_2$ for the projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. With $T^\vee=\mathcal Hom(T,\mathcal O_H)$ and tensor products of module sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the invertible module $$D(T)=m^*T\otimes(p_1^*T)^\vee\otimes(p_2^*T)^\vee$$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{H\times_kH}$. All pullbacks are tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback]. The asserted isomorphism is over $k$; it is not merely an isomorphism after algebraic closure. No multiplication, coherence condition, or normalization of an isomorphism is included in this assertion.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality] with $n=1$, $H_{\bar k}$ is integral and in particular connected. Thus $H$ is geometrically connected, i.e. connected after every field extension, by [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure]. Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-semiabelian-split-quotient] to obtain a finite Galois extension $K/k$ and a split-torus torsor homomorphism $q:H_K\to A$ onto an abelian variety over $K$. Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-line-pullback] to $q$ and $T_K$: its base $A$ is smooth, separated and of finite type. Obtain an invertible module $N$ on $A$ with $q^*N\simeq T_K$.

source.place: I Propositions 8.4 and 9.3; agent assembly for a split-torus extension

proof.text: Work over an algebraic closure $F$ of $k$ containing $K$. Choose the finite chain of families in the hypothesis, oriented from $\mathcal O$ to $T_F$. For each link, let $\mathcal L_j$ on $H_F\times V_j$ have endpoint classes $L_{j-1},L_j$. The base change $q\times1:H_F\times V_j\to A_F\times V_j$ is a split-torus torsor over a smooth separated finite-type $F$-scheme. These product properties follow directly: combine finite presentations and formal-smoothness lifts componentwise, and cut out the product diagonal by the two pulled-back diagonal ideals. By [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-line-pullback], $\mathcal L_j\simeq(q\times1)^*\mathcal M_j$ for a line $\mathcal M_j$ on $A_F\times V_j$. Put $M=\bigotimes_j(\mathcal M_{j,b_j}\otimes\mathcal M_{j,a_j}^{\vee})$. Each factor is algebraically trivial: tensor its defining family by the inverse of the constant initial fibre. Tensor products and inverses preserve the generated equivalence relation by tensoring the families. Hence $M$ is algebraically trivial and $q_F^*M\simeq T_F$ by cancellation of adjacent endpoints. Pullback commutes with tensor and composition by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]; its compatibility with duals follows by pulling back evaluation and checking on a local frame. Therefore $q_F^*(N_F\otimes M^\vee)\simeq\mathcal O$. By [lem-sfb-semiabelian-picard-pullback-kernel], $N_F\otimes M^\vee$ is algebraically trivial. Consequently $N_F$ is algebraically trivial.

source.place: I Propositions 8.4 and 9.3; agent assembly for a split-torus extension

proof.text: Regard $A$ as a commutative group algebraic space over the Noetherian scheme $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$ by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]; the identity chart is an etale atlas, so $A\to S$ is proper, smooth and of finite presentation. For each algebraically closed $\Omega\supseteq K$, $A_\Omega$ is a proper smooth group scheme, connected since $A$ is geometrically integral by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization]. $\Omega$ contains an algebraic closure of $K$, which is $K$-isomorphic to $F$. Base change the chain of Step 2 showing $N_F$ algebraically trivial along $F\to\Omega$: each parameter $V_\Omega$ is smooth, separated, of finite type and connected, by [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] since $V$ is connected over the algebraically closed $F$, and fibres at $F$-points base change to fibres at $\Omega$-points. So $N_\Omega$ is algebraically trivial on every geometric fibre. Choose a rigidification $e^*N\simeq K$ of the one-dimensional $K$-space $e^*N$. By [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison], $N$ and its pullbacks and tensor products are the line modules of [lem-sfb-algebraically-trivial-line-multiplicativity] (tensor, dual and pullback have the same transition units on both sites), and isomorphisms of line modules come from isomorphisms of invertible modules. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraically-trivial-line-multiplicativity] with $T=S$, $M=N$: $m_A^*N\simeq p_1^*N\otimes p_2^*N$ over $K$ itself. Since $q$ is a homomorphism, $q m_H=m_A(q\times q)$ and $q p_i=p_i(q\times q)$. Pull back this isomorphism along $q\times q$, use $q^*N\simeq T_K$ and [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], and cancel each line against its dual using evaluation. This gives a trivialization $\tau:D(T)_K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O$ over $K$.

source.place: I Proposition 8.4, printed pp.35--36 (theorem of the square for Picard-zero lines), via the existing DAG node lem-sfb-algebraically-trivial-line-multiplicativity; agent assembly for a split-torus extension

proof.text: Choose a basis of the one-dimensional $k$-space $e^*T$. On either identity axis of $H\times H$, evaluation cancels $T$ against $T^\vee$, leaving the constant line $(e^*T)^\vee$. The chosen basis therefore gives two $k$-defined axis trivializations of $D(T)$ that agree at $(e,e)$. Relative to these, the restrictions of $\tau$ are units $a,b$ on $H_K$ with $a(e)=b(e)=c\in K^\times$. Replace $\tau$ by $\tau/(p_1^*a\,p_2^*b/c)$. It now agrees with both prescribed axis trivializations. For each $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$, $\sigma(\tau)/\tau$ is a unit on $H_K^2$ equal to $1$ on both axes. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-group-unit-axis-factorization] over the reduced base $\operatorname{Spec}K$, with $n=2$: that unit is $1$. Thus $\tau$ is Galois invariant.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, identity (79), and Remark 12.50; agent axis normalization

proof.text: The tensor decomposition in [lem-exc-finite-galois-tensor-decomposition](1), followed by [lem-exc-finite-galois-algebra-tensor-decomposition], identifies the overlap $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_kK)$ with copies of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ whose two maps are the identity and $\operatorname{Spec}\sigma$. Hence the invariance just proved says exactly that the two pullbacks of $\tau$ to the overlap agree, with the canonical descent datum of the $k$-line $D(T)$. The projection $(H\times H)_K\to H\times H$ is an fpqc covering: a finite nonzero free field extension stays finite faithfully flat after base change. Apply the compatible-trivialization clause (3) of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] to obtain $D(T)\simeq\mathcal O_{H\times H}$ over $k$.
